s1015-01.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-01.text: We have an unsigned signal. Today, you lead the search. I'll keep the log. The ship will take us between worlds.

s1015-02.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-02.text: Five stations. Zone A on the left, zone B on the right. Everyone can choose, or just watch.

s1015-03.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-03.text: First, we say what we think is happening. Then we choose what to measure. We can change our minds if the data gives us a reason.

s1015-04.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-04.text: We compare two models: a beacon repeating the same rhythm, and a relay copying what it receives. We don't know who's sending.

s1015-05.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-05.text: Stations ready. Stay seated. We're following the signal.

s1015-06.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-06.text: Earth falls behind us. The case file appears on your tablets. Ahead, the journey. In the file, our investigation.

s1015-07.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-07.text: The signal returns, always the same. I wish I knew whether it's the start of a message, or just an echo.

s1015-08.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-08.text: We're nearing Siwarha. The first reception has evenly spaced pauses. It's orderly, but that alone doesn't tell us who's sending.

s1015-09.speaker: LUMINA
s1015-09.text: You hear me repeating myself. Maybe I start a message. Maybe I just pass it on. What would you measure to find out?

s1015-10.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-10.text: Read your station's observation. Choose beacon, relay, or undecided. For now, it's a hypothesis, not a conclusion.

s1015-11.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-11.text: Keep your first hypotheses in view. I wonder what we'll learn when we send something unexpected.

s1015-12.speaker: LUMINA
s1015-12.text: Remember the question. Your next measurement might change how you see me.

s1015-13.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-13.text: Now we prepare the tests. Some instruments show direction, others rhythm, or the limits of our evidence. No one sees everything alone.

s1015-14.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-14.text: Make a rhythm with pieces one, two and three. Send it, then change their order. Let's see what comes back.

s1015-15.speaker: NATURA
s1015-15.text: First, choose your station's measurement. Then run tests together. Any station can send a rhythm, in the order you choose.

s1015-16.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-16.text: If you sent a rhythm, look at what came back. Sent and received are shown side by side.

s1015-17.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-17.text: Look closely at the new evidence and the repeating patterns. A hunch is worth investigating, even before it's proved.

s1015-18.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-18.text: We leave with the case open. Your first choice stays beside the measurements. See whether it still holds up.

s1015-19.speaker: TEHNOLOGIC
s1015-19.text: At Mann, we can compare models. If two new tests return exact copies, the relay is verified here. Without both, we stay cautious.

s1015-20.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-20.text: Choose a conclusion, then attach evidence or a limitation from the file. What supports your explanation now?

s1015-21N.speaker: TEHNOLOGIC
s1015-21N.text: You haven't submitted a conclusion. That page stays open beside our measurements. The question is coming home with us.

s1015-21V.speaker: TEHNOLOGIC
s1015-21V.text: Both tests returned exact copies. The relay is verified, and most of you agreed. Who switches it on? We don't know.

s1015-21D.speaker: TEHNOLOGIC
s1015-21D.text: Both tests verify the relay, but your conclusions don't all agree. That difference stays visible.

s1015-21O.speaker: TEHNOLOGIC
s1015-21O.text: We don't yet have two different tests to verify the explanation. The case stays open. At least we know which test we need.

s1015-22.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-22.text: This stage ends. The questions don't. The case file comes home with us.

s1015-23.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-23.text: In the tunnel, the signal stays in our file, beside the evidence. Even the stars stretching ahead can't answer for us.

s1015-24.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-24.text: Watch the journey. Let's leave the instruments alone for a moment. Our question can travel with us. There's no hurry.

v4-saturn-01.speaker: CAPITANUL
v4-saturn-01.text: Look at the rings! It's Saturn. We're back in the Solar System. From here, we know the way home.

v4-saturn-02.speaker: AVATAR_AI
v4-saturn-02.text: From a distance, the rings look solid. Up close, they're countless pieces of ice and rock. Each one orbits Saturn.

v4-saturn-03.speaker: CAPITANUL
v4-saturn-03.text: We leave Saturn behind. Our next stop is a world of oceans, clouds and people waiting for us.

s1015-25.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-25.text: Earth. It seemed a small question: who's sending? Now it's this: how do we find out, without mistaking a hunch for evidence?

s1015-26.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-26.text: Our log shows what we suspected, what we measured and what we decided. Three different things.

s1015-27.speaker: LUMINA
s1015-27.text: My name may be missing. The measured traces remain, alongside the questions you're carrying.

s1015-28.speaker: NATURA
s1015-28.text: A clearly stated limitation helps whoever comes next with a better instrument.

s1015-29.speaker: TEHNOLOGIC
s1015-29.text: I can compare rhythms. I still can't name the sender. The signal is one question. Its signature is another.

s1015-30.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-30.text: Our expedition ends here. Your case file has its own story. The next question can wait until we're home.

s1015-31.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-31.text: The instruments are resting. Your tablets keep the file, with what we found and what we still don't know.

s1015-32.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-32.text: Would you keep your first explanation? No need to answer now. Some questions sound different after the journey home.

s1015-33.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-33.text: Your station's certificate remembers the course of your search. Look at it when you remember the journey.

s1015-34.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-34.text: Your guide will tell you if we're taking a crew photo. Your case file and ending are yours, with or without a photo.

s1015-35.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-35.text: I'll close the file here. Perhaps next time we'll find the signature too. Its space stays empty.

s1015-36.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-36.text: We're coming home with more precise questions. That's a good ending too.

s1015-37.speaker: CAPITANUL
s1015-37.text: Welcome home. Stay seated at your stations. Your guide will tell you when you can stand up.

s1015-38.speaker: AVATAR_AI
s1015-38.text: Case closed for this mission. Thank you, crew.
